Triggers.value: Being in a natural environment similar to where it happened

Maladaptive Strategies.value: cut off all contact with friends and family
I drink alcohol, take medication or use drugs

Threat.value: I am unable to relax even when I know I am in a safe place
When something takes longer than expected I assume something bad is happening

Negative Appraisals.value: I feel guilty for surviving when others did not
I feel isolated and set apart from others
I acted in ways that go against who I am

vignette: John, a 47-year-old African American park ranger living in California, has been struggling with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) since his time spent in a war-torn region of Africa several years ago. The traumatic event that haunts him was when he witnessed the brutal attack on fellow civilians by armed combatants while he was delivering humanitarian aid. Being criticized or corrected during this mission triggered intense anxiety, as it reminded him of the criticism he received for not being able to protect those around him. Whenever John is in a natural environment similar to where the incident took place, such as his work as a park ranger, he feels a rush of panic and fear. The sight of fire or flames immediately brings back vivid memories of the infernos during the attack. These triggers have led him to engage in maladaptive strategies like isolating completely from friends and family and using substances to numb his overwhelming emotions. The more John isolates himself, the deeper he sinks into a cycle of guilt and isolation. He often finds it difficult to relax even when he knows he is safe, and any delay or unexpected event triggers his assumption that something bad is happening again. This constant state of hyper-vigilance exacerbates his sleep problems, as he lies awake, ruminating on the events in Africa. John’s survival guilt weighs heavily on him; he feels deeply responsible for not being able to save others during the attack. This guilt has led to a pervasive sense of isolation and feeling set apart from others, further reinforcing his belief that something bad will happen if he is in a situation similar to where it happened before. His negative appraisals also lead to an increased threat perception, as he constantly feels vulnerable and unsafe. His substance use, primarily drinking alcohol to cope with the anxiety and guilt, has led to deteriorating relationships at work and home. He often misses critical meetings due to hangovers or is unable to concentrate on his duties. The maladaptive strategies only reinforce his negative appraisals, creating a self-perpetuating cycle of isolation, substance use, and increased threat perception. John’s avoidance behaviors have extended beyond his personal life into his professional environment. Being around military uniforms or weapons triggers strong memories that make him feel unsafe and paranoid. As a result, he has started to avoid areas in the park where uniformed security personnel are present, leading to strained relationships with colleagues who depend on his leadership. The accumulation of these behaviors has led to significant occupational consequences. John’s work performance has declined, and he has been under scrutiny from supervisors for missing critical duties and deadlines. This scrutiny triggers more anxiety and guilt, further exacerbating his PTSD symptoms. John had come to believe that no one could truly understand what he went through, so he isolated himself even more, cutting off contact with friends and family who tried to reach out. What frightened him most was the prospect of reliving those traumatic moments in Africa, and this fear often led him to drink excessively or use drugs as a way to cope. John finally sought help after his performance at work reached a critical point, and he faced possible termination if he did not address his issues. He is most afraid that his past will continue to haunt him, making it impossible for him to move forward in life. However, he also holds hope that through therapy, he can find ways to manage his symptoms and regain some sense of normalcy and peace.
